title: Windows with focus that are not on top are minimized when clicked in the task manager
line: Clicking the task of an active window that is partly covered by another window now raises it instead of minimizing it.
explanation: activateTask() in TaskTools.js minimized any active task when "Clicking active task: Minimizes" was on, without looking at the stacking order. With focus follows mouse (or anything else that focuses a window without raising it) the active window can be covered by others, so a click meant to bring it up hid it instead. The new isCoveredByOtherWindow() helper checks whether a non-minimized window higher in the stacking order, on the current desktop and activity, overlaps the clicked one (ignoring keep-above windows the clicked one can't rise above); in that case the click raises the window, otherwise it still minimizes.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: raise active task covered by other windows on click

With focus follows mouse the active window can sit below other windows,
and clicking its task minimized it instead of bringing it up. Now the
click only minimizes when no window that it can rise above overlaps it.

BUG: 365948

media.caption: Clicking Dolphin's task now raises it above Konsole

review.text: Checking stacking order, window layer (KeepAbove/KeepBelow), virtual desktop, activity, and geometry overlap in `TaskTools.js` before minimizing an active window is a clean, well-scoped fix for focus-follows-mouse users. However, `covers(other)` does not filter out non-window model entries (`IsWindow`), so a startup item (`StartupTasksModel`) returning `undefined` for `StackingOrder` and `VirtualDesktops` bypasses `<= stackingOrder` (since `undefined <= n` is `false` in JS) and throws an uncaught `TypeError` on `desktops.indexOf(...)`, breaking clicks on active tasks while an app is launching. The geometry and role checks should also guard against undefined or empty `(0,0,0,0)` rects.
changes: Skip non-window items at the start of `covers(other)` by checking `!data(other, TaskManager.AbstractTasksModel.IsWindow)` so pinned launchers and startup notifications are never inspected as covering windows.

Guard against undefined/invalid role values in `isCoveredByOtherWindow()` (check `typeof stackingOrder === "number"`, `typeof otherStackingOrder === "number"`, non-null `desktops`/`activities`, and `width > 0 && height > 0` on both `geometry` and `otherGeometry` so empty `(0,0,0,0)` rects cannot falsely overlap a window spanning `(0,0)`).

reviews.text: Fixes exactly what the reporter and Nate describe: an active but covered window (focus follows mouse) is now raised on click instead of minimized, and still minimizes once it is on top. The check lives in the right place (activateTask's minimize branch) and uses existing libtaskmanager roles (StackingOrder, Geometry, keep-above/below layer, desktop/activity filtering), with sensible handling of group children and keep-above windows that would otherwise cause a raise-forever loop. Screenshots clearly show Dolphin minimized before and raised above Konsole after; commit message, line and explanation match the diff. A maintainer might prefer the overlap helper in C++ on TasksModel, but the QML/JS version is self-contained and cherry-pickable.
